recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + Audit foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency foundation. shared-types enums (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, UserRole) are consumed by every other module. Audit module has no domain dependencies and is needed by all state-changing operations per GP-002.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Leave Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Defines entitlement rules that leave-balance and leave-request both consume. Must exist before balances can be initialized or requests validated.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-policy and audit. Owns the balance lifecycle (initialize, deduct-pending, commit, restore). Must exist before leave-request can submit/approve/reject.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Leave Request module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-balance, leave-policy, and audit. Orchestrates the full request lifecycle: validate → submit (deduct pending) → approve (commit) / reject (restore). This is the largest module.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Routes, controllers, and RBAC wiring
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all domain modules. Fastify route registration, controller layer, auth middleware integration, and RBAC guards. Exposes the REST API surface.

app_notes: Application layer design for the leave management module. Four domain modules (leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit) plus shared-types. Dependencies flow inward: leave-request → leave-balance → leave-policy → shared-types, with audit as a cross-cutting dependency consumed by both leave-balance and leave-request. All state-changing operations go through repository interfaces and produce audit records (GP-001, GP-002). RBAC enforced at route level via middleware (GP-005). Balance lifecycle uses a pending-deduct-commit pattern: submit deducts from pending, approve commits the deduction, reject restores pending. Three open questions recorded for carryover policy, emergency leave accounting, and balance computation strategy.

open_questions.question: How should unused annual leave be handled at fiscal-year rollover — carry over fully, carry over with a cap, or expire?
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveBalanceService.initializeBalance for the new fiscal year and LeavePolicy entity shape (may need a maxCarryoverDays field).
candidate_options: Full carryover: unused entitled days roll into next year's entitled pool
Capped carryover: carry over up to N days (configurable per policy)
Use-it-or-lose-it: unused days expire at fiscal year end

open_questions.question: Should emergency leave be drawn from the same annual/sick balance pools, or is it a separate entitlement with its own policy rules?
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveBalanceService.deductPending — if emergency leave has its own pool, a separate balance row is needed; if it draws from annual/sick, the deduction logic must choose which pool to debit.
candidate_options: Separate pool: emergency leave has its own entitlement and balance tracking
Draws from annual: emergency leave debits the annual leave balance
Draws from sick: emergency leave debits the sick leave balance
Configurable: the policy specifies which pool emergency leave draws from

open_questions.question: What is the binding computation for available balance — entitled minus (used + pending), or entitled minus used only?
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveBalanceService.recalculateAvailable and the validation in LeaveRequestService.validateRequest. The choice determines whether pending requests block new submissions for the same days.
candidate_options: entitled - (used + pending): pending requests consume balance immediately, preventing double-booking
entitled - used: pending requests do not reduce available balance, allowing overlapping submissions

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } — UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. JWT bearer token verified by auth middleware (Fastify preHandler hook) that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by requireRole(...) route-level guard, never inline. Employees submit/cancel their own requests; managers approve/reject requests for their direct reports; hr_admin can configure policies and view all balances.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (code: VALIDATION_ERROR). Authentication failure → 401 (code: UNAUTHORIZED). Authorization failure → 403 (code: FORBIDDEN). Not found → 404 (code: NOT_FOUND). Insufficient balance → 422 (code: INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE). Policy violation (e.g. exceeds max consecutive days) → 422 (code: POLICY_VIOLATION).
